handling.guidance: One declared start. The episode is a stretch of attention on one topic, said by the person; it is not inferred from mind.attention readings, so a run of readings opens nothing. topic is the spelling mind.attention fixes (deskcam), and it is the series key: the latest started of a topic is the open one, and mind.attention.ended closes it. A topic returned to later gets a new started. at is the minute it began, as a wall clock in Australia/Sydney or at the offset source_time names. The id is declared in identity_template, <source>:attention/<topic>/started/<at as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM>, then source_time's offset, so leave id out and Anam fills it; send it and it must match.

schema.description: The moment the person says a topic began to hold their attention, opening an episode of that topic. Said by the person, through a conversation or the Workbench, and never worked out from readings. mind.attention.ended with the same topic closes it; a later started of that topic opens a new one.

at.description: When the person said attention on the topic began, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM as a wall clock in Australia/Sydney, or at the offset source_time names. This is the fact time.

topic.description: What the attention is on, in one agreed spelling: lower case, words joined by hyphens, the way a drug has one spelling. A project, a subject or an activity, named as the person already names it, so the same thing is always the same string. It is the key of the mind.attention episode series, so mind.attention.ended with the same topic closes it.

id.description: Identity, composed from the rest by the Definition's identity_template: the source prefix, then attention, the topic and the moment, then the offset source_time names. A writer may leave it out and Anam fills it; one that sends it must send exactly the composition.

note.description: Free text in the person's words, about the start of this stretch of attention.

source_time.description: How `at` was read: value is the wall clock as the person said it, zone the zone it was said in (an IANA name when the writer knows one, else the offset again), offset the offset from UTC it had then, and basis who decided the zone (source when the person's own client or browser names it, configuration when the writer's setting does). The fact time is `at` read at offset.

value.description: The fact time as the source supplied it, as text and never rewritten: a date, a wall clock, an RFC 3339 string, or an epoch as its digits.

zone.description: The zone value is read in, and nothing else: an IANA name when one is known, UTC for a value that is UTC, else a fixed offset +HH:MM or -HH:MM. The gate refuses a name that is no zone.

offset.description: The offset from UTC value had at that moment in zone, +HH:MM or -HH:MM, which names one instant even in an hour the zone repeats. A writer that cannot tell it refuses rather than guess.

basis.description: Who decided the zone. source: the source supplied it with the value, or the value is UTC by the source's own definition. configuration: a setting a person made for this source names it. assumption: the importer or writer chose it, with nothing behind it but its own default or the Definition's zone, and logged that it did.
